text: One hot summer afternoon, as a black thunderstorm was coming up, Tom was about to ruin a poor land speculator, who begged him for a few more months. <break time="0.8s" /> You have made so much money out of me, said the speculator, and at these words Tom lost both his patience and his piety. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil take me, said he, if I have made a farthing. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then there were three loud knocks at the street door, and when Tom stepped out, there stood the dark man holding a black horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom, I have come for you, said the visitor gruffly, and never was a sinner taken more by surprise. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom shrank back, but it was too late, for he had left his little Bible in his coat pocket and his big one buried under the mortgage on his desk. <break time="0.8s" /> The dark man lifted him like a child into the saddle, and away they galloped toward the swamp, the thunder roaring all around them. <break time="0.8s" /> Afterward his bonds and mortgages were found burned to ashes, his iron chest held only wood chips, and his house burned to the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Such was the end of Tom Walker, whose ghost, it is said, still haunts the swamp on stormy nights, riding a horse in his white cap.
